title: A Community‐Centred Approach to Climate Adaptation Planning for Biodiversity: Lessons for Stakeholder Learning From a Case Study in the Northern Rivers Region of New South Wales, Australia
content:
The findings from this study show how a deliberately designed participatory planning process—integrating local knowledge, tailored scientific data on climate hazards, ecological assessment frameworks and decision-support tools—can build stakeholder capacity for climate adaptation planning for biodiversity. Through a series of six workshops, participants developed a shared understanding of climate risks, species vulnerabilities and adaptation options, and evaluated their feasibility and robustness under contrasting socio-ecological scenarios. Learning emerged through structured deliberation, repeated tool use and collaborative engagement. The findings emphasise that aligning process design with analytical tools can support climate adaptation decision-making in complex and uncertain contexts.


ABSTRACT

Climate change is intensifying pressures on biodiversity, creating complex and uncertain socio-ecological challenges for conservation. Participatory planning processes are widely advocated, yet empirical evidence on effective design remains limited. This study reports on findings from a community-centred workshop series on adaptation planning for biodiversity in Australia's Northern Rivers region. Findings show how iterative, deliberately designed processes integrating tailored climate and ecological data, stakeholder knowledge and decision-support tools can build practical capacity for adaptation planning and offer transferable insights for other regions.
